key_insight: The paper introduces a standardized benchmarking framework that enables objective, reproducible evaluation of neuromorphic controllers on soft robotic platforms. It unifies tasks, metrics and deployment protocols to bridge simulation and physical embodiment for neuromorphic agents.
problem_solved: There was no common, reproducible way to compare neuromorphic controllers in soft embodied systems, making it hard to evaluate progress, generalization, and hardware–software co‑design across labs and platforms.
method: Define a benchmark suite of embodied tasks and performance metrics tailored to soft robotics and neuromorphic controllers.
Provide standard protocols for simulation-to-hardware evaluation and repeatable experimental procedures across platforms.
Integrate tools and interfaces to run, log and compare neuromorphic controllers on real soft robots and corresponding simulators.
impact: This framework lets researchers and practitioners fairly compare neuromorphic algorithms and hardware, improving reproducibility and accelerating design choices for embodied AI and neuromorphic systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: benchmark workflow from task definition → neuromorphic controller → simulator → physical soft robot → metrics
Task grid: icons representing the suite of embodied tasks (locomotion, manipulation, compliance, sensing)
Performance radar/comparison chart: multi-metric comparisons across controllers and hardware (latency, energy, robustness, accuracy)
Schematic showing sim-to-hardware transfer with arrows and checklist for reproducible protocols
paper_title: A benchmarking framework for embodied neuromorphic agents
paper_authors: Giulia D’Angelo, Jens E. Pedersen, Taimoor Hassan, Matteo Cianchetti, Josh Bongard
